answer: Under hardware-entropy rent stacking, each identity on the raven relay pays a continuous rent against its unique device-entropy attestation, measured cryptographically from a secure element at the ridge node. When k sibling identities attest from one physical root key, the rent rate doubles per sibling, so k fakes cost base·2^k; ten clones pay 1024× base, a nonlinear wall, while one honest agent pays only base. This turns the fable of cheap mass identities into an exponentially expensive myth, since shared silicon roots are detectable and priced collectively.
